output.summary: A perennial wetland plant native across most of Eurasia and North America, and more locally in Africa and South America. Its adjoining male and female flower sections develop into the familiar brown, sausage-shaped seed head, which persists through winter before breaking apart in spring.
output.edibilityNote: Rhizomes require cooking and skinning; peeled stems and leaf bases may be raw or cooked. Young spikes, shoots and sprouts are edible; avoid polluted or bitter specimens.
